newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PT Tambang Timah awaiting Busang deadline.
newsitem.headline: PT Tambang Timah awaiting Busang deadline.

text.p: Indonesia's PT Tambang Timah said on Tuesday it was awaiting a deadline given to two Canadian mining companies to settle with local partners over the huge Busang gold find before seeking a stake in the project.
"We are awaiting the deadline to see what will happen," Tambang Timah President Director Erry Riyana Hardjapamekas told a news conference in announcing the 1996 results.
Tambang Timah, the world's largest integrated tin miner, has expressed an interest in taking a stake in the Busang find, estimated to contain more than 57 million ounces of gold.

The government has given Canadian miners Bre-X Minerals Ltd and Barrick Gold Corp to mid-February to reach agreements with their Indonesian partners before getting the go-ahead to further explore and develop Busang.
Placer Dome Inc is among other firms who have expressed an interest in Busang.
Tambang Timah said earlier on Tuesday it had government approval to explore for gold deposits in Sumatra, Kalimantan and East Java.

"The government agreed in principle late last year to allow us to explore for gold along the southern coast of East Java. This has brought our gold exploration areas to around seven so far," corporate secretary Prasetyo B. Saksono told Reuters.
Saksono said Timah, also listed in London, also had the right to explore for gold in five areas in Kalimantan on Borneo island and one area in North Sumatra.
Saksono declined to give details on the exploration work, saying the firm allocated around five billion rupiah annually for exploration. It has not so far produced any gold.
